title: Task Complexity
measures: How demanding the tasks assigned to the student were, so that a student who took on hard tasks is not compared with one who took easy ones.
inputs: story points and subtasks of the student's tasks
files the tasks touch and how many files depend on them before the sprint (import graph)
total story points of the sprint
computation: Ridge on the proposal's five features plus the total story points assigned in the sprint (log). Score 0-1.
gates: Available as soon as tasks are assigned (it describes the plan and the code before the work).
validation: 144 real student-sprints, student-disjoint 5-fold CV against assistant-written ratings: MAE 0.087 (mean predictor 0.145). All of the signal is the sprint's total story points; the model is NOT shown to beat that one feature (gain 0.004, interval [-0.001, 0.010]); the code-based features add nothing measurable. The rater saw story points, so the relation may reflect the rubric as much as difficulty.
limits: Story points are the team's own estimates and can be inflated.
Import-graph reach works for relative imports in JavaScript/TypeScript/Dart and by class name in Java/Kotlin; monorepos and aliases are missed.

warnings.not shown to beat: The score is, in effect, the story-point total; do not read more into it.

typical_problems.symptom: complexity high for a student with few tasks
typical_problems.likely_cause: one task with many story points
